newsitem.title: INDIA: Investors want bolder India reforms.
newsitem.headline: Investors want bolder India reforms.

text.p: India must focus on keeping its economic reforms on track to restore investor confidence in its volatile stock markets, rather than just offering cosmetic help, foreign investors said on Thursday.
"The government should be letting market forces act. They shouldn't be tampering and certainly not in equity markets," said the head of sales at a London-based securities house.

Bombay's benchmark stocks index has risen more than 15 percent this month on assurances by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram that they would announce a large package of measures to boost capital markets.
The package is expected before Deve Gowda leaves for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, on Friday.
But investors said the expected measures were likely to be short-sighted and drew attention away from macroeconomic worries like a growing fiscal deficit and a slowdown in industrial growth.

"I'm hoping to see a well-thought-out strategy for domestic debt reduction and a strategy for improving public sector performance," said a Hong Kong-based economist at a U.S. investment bank. "I don't think a cosmetic package will help."
Analysts said diluting the recently introduced minimum alternate tax (MAT) on previously untaxed company profits -- an expected measure -- would be a grave mistake.
"The removal of MAT or its replacement by something less effective would be terribly disastrous," said the head of sales at the London-based securities firm.
"The government needs to raise tax revenues and it would be a mistake to withdraw MAT," the economist said.
Analysts said wary investors were using the current stocks rally to offload index heavyweights.
"A lot of people are selling into this rally, and those that don't want to sell are waiting for the crash to buy back," said the chief dealer at a European brokerage.
Some analysts said the government should turn its attention to attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) -- the key to financing the country's burgeoning infrastructure needs.
"The government should focus on FDI instead of trying to boost the index," said Partha Roy Choudhury, assistant director, equity trading, at Peregrine Brokerage Ltd in Hong Kong.

"In fact, recently the government's focus has been and is likely to continue to be to encourage direct investment," Choudhury said, referring to announcements aimed at boosting investment in core sectors such as power, telecommunications and ports.
"I have never believed that they will offer any outlandish incentives to the markets," he said.
